string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing, the capital of the People's Republic of China, is the country's political, cultural and educational centre. As one of the four direct-controlled municipalities, it is home to more than twenty-one million residents. Its history stretches back over three millennia, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites include the Great Wall, the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and the Summer Palace. For centuries Beijing was the capital of the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties, and its grid-like old city still reflects that imperial planning. Today it is a sprawling modern metropolis that hosted the 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games, balancing historic hutong alleyways with a booming technology and finance sector.

Shanghai is China's largest city and a global centre for finance, trade and shipping. It sits on the estuary of the Yangtze River on the country's central coast and is one of the four direct-controlled municipalities, with nearly twenty-five million residents. Once a modest fishing town, Shanghai grew into one of the world's busiest ports during the nineteenth century, and its famous Bund preserves a row of grand colonial-era buildings. Today the skyline of Pudong, dominated by the Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower, symbolises China's rapid economic rise. The city blends Art Deco landmarks, traditional shikumen lane houses and a thriving arts and culinary scene.

Chongqing is a direct-controlled municipality in southwest China and the most populous city by administrative area in the country. It sits where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet, its clusters of skyscrapers climbing steep hillsides above the water, which has earned it the nickname the 'Mountain City'. Formerly part of Sichuan province, Chongqing became a municipality in 1997 to drive development in China's interior. It is a major industrial, manufacturing and transport hub and the traditional starting point for cruises through the Three Gorges. The city is also famous for its spicy hotpot, its famously misty weather and the dramatic river landscapes that surround it.

Tianjin is one of China's four direct-controlled municipalities, located on the coast of the Bohai Sea about thirty kilometres southeast of Beijing. It grew up along the Grand Canal and became a northern trading port; after it opened as a treaty port, foreign concessions left a distinctive legacy of European and Italian architecture. Its historic Fifth Avenue district and the Italian-style town are now popular attractions. Today Tianjin is a major industrial base, home to one of the world's largest container ports and a busy free-trade zone. It is also a centre for higher education, and its food culture is known for crispy mahua fried dough twists and jianbing street breakfasts.
